theorem.statement:
For every fixed \(K\) and \(b\), the handle \(\mathfrak C\) has a Turing-model implementation with the following guarantee.  Given any rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary entries and menus constant in \(a\), any rational contrast \(c\), any size profile \(s\), and any rational \(\varepsilon>0\), it constructs the exact rational orbit kernel \(H\), weakly optimizes \(\mathsf P\) and \(\mathsf Q\), and returns a rational implementable design \(D\), a rational endpoint estimator table \(\delta\), a rational least-favorable-prior certificate, and rational numbers \(\underline R,\overline R\) such that
\[
 \underline R\le R^\star\le\overline R,
 \qquad \overline R-\underline R\le\varepsilon.
\]
Its running time is polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size, the rational input bit length, and \(\log\max\{2,1/\varepsilon\}\).  It also returns a polynomial-size division-free rational arithmetic recursion for the continuous-outcome extension of \(\delta\); the recursion detects rational zero-likelihood cells exactly and has a total mathematical interpretation for every real revealed vector, including every zero-design-mass or zero-prior-likelihood face.  The guarantee is weak approximation and makes no assertion that an exact optimizer has rational coordinates.
theorem.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 J=|\mathcal N|,
 \qquad A=|\mathcal K|,
 \qquad
 M=\#\{(n,\omega):\omega\text{ is compatible with }n\}.
\tag{1}
\]
All three integers are bounded by the displayed orbit-program size.  Because \(m\ge1\) and \(K\ge2\), assigning all clusters either of two distinct labels gives two assignment orbits, so \(J\ge2\).  The all-zero and all-one binary schedules give two distinct response orbits, so \(A\ge2\).  Thus both reduced-coordinate spaces used below have positive dimension.  We prove the claim in five steps.

\emph{Step 1: exact construction and bit growth of the orbit experiment.}
For a size-\(q\) cluster, a complete binary response word has \(2K\) bits, so there are \(2^{2K}\) words and
\[
 B_q=\binom{q+2^{2K}-1}{q}
\tag{2}
\]
unordered cluster response types.  They can be generated lexicographically.  The number of local observation categories is
\[
 O_q=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}(r_{q,a}+1)(q-r_{q,a}+1).
\tag{3}
\]
For each type \(t\), label \(a\), and category \((u,v)\), the numerator in \(P_{t,a}(u,v)\) is found by testing the at most \(2^b\) subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,q\}\); its denominator is the positive integer \(\binom q{r_{q,a}}\).  This denominator equals one when \(r_{q,a}=0\) or \(q\), so this calculation neither divides by zero nor uses an interior-count condition.  The subsets are partitioned by \((u,v)\), whence
\[
 P_{t,a}(u,v)\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{u=0}^{r_{q,a}}\sum_{v=0}^{q-r_{q,a}}P_{t,a}(u,v)=1.
\tag{4}
\]

For a response histogram \(\kappa\), compute the coefficients of \(F_{\kappa,q}\) from \(\texttt{def:orbit-kernel}\) by inserting one cluster factor at a time.  After \(j\) factors, the dynamic-programming state is an \(O_q\)-vector of nonnegative counts having total degree \(j\); hence there are at most
\[
 \binom{j+O_q-1}{O_q-1}\le (m_q+1)^{O_q}
\tag{5}
\]
states, and each update has at most \(O_q\) outgoing transitions.  The label margins of a state determine \(n\).  Dividing a terminal coefficient by the positive multinomial
\(\binom{m_q}{(n_{q,a})_{a\in\mathcal A}}\), and multiplying over \(q\), gives exactly \(H_{\kappa n\omega}\).  Indeed, the coefficient sums the product subset probabilities over all allocations of the specified local triples, and the multinomial is exactly the number of equally likely label allocations.  Summing over all compatible \(\omega\) and using (4) gives
\[
 H_{\kappa n\omega}\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{\omega}H_{\kappa n\omega}=1
 \quad\text{for every }(\kappa,n).
\tag{6}
\]
Incompatible margins are recognized by integer comparison and assigned probability zero.  Thus the computation preserves the full exact-count observation histogram; it does not replace it by a pairwise conflict graph.

Because \(K\) and \(b\) are fixed, the alphabets in (2)--(3) are fixed.  A product of at most \(m\) local denominators has \(O(m)\) bits, a multinomial has \(O(m\log(m+1))\) bits, and every coefficient numerator is no larger than the common denominator times the number of paths, whose logarithm is \(O(m)\).  Standard integer addition, multiplication, greatest-common-divisor reduction, and exact division therefore keep every intermediate rational at bit length polynomial in the input length and \(m\).  Equations (2), (3), and (5) show that enumerating all orbit indices and all entries of \(H\) takes a number of bit operations polynomial in the displayed table size and the input bit length.  Finally, \(\theta_\kappa\) is obtained by an integer histogram sum followed by multiplication by the rational coefficients \(c_{z,a}\) and division by the positive integer \(N\); hence it too is computed exactly with polynomial bit length.  Since \(\sum_{z,a}c_{z,a}=0\), the positive and negative coefficient sums both equal \(L\), and bounded outcomes give
\[
 |\theta_\kappa|\le L.
\tag{7}
\]
The nonzero contrast makes \(L>0\).

\emph{Step 2: the exact global primal oracle and explicit containing bodies.}
For rational \((d,t)\in\mathbb R^2\) and \(\theta\in[-L,L]\), define on the entire plane
\[
 \Phi_\theta(d,t)
 =\max_{u\in[-L,L]}
 \bigl\{(2u-2\theta)t+(\theta^2-u^2)d\bigr\}.
\tag{8}
\]
This is a maximum of affine functions of \((d,t)\), so it is globally finite and convex.  It has an exact rational evaluation at every rational ambient query.  If \(d>0\), the quadratic in \(u\) is concave and a maximizer is
\[
 u^\star=\max\{-L,\min\{L,t/d\}\}.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(d\le0\), the quadratic is convex or affine, so one evaluates its two rational endpoint values and chooses the larger.  Thus (8) uses only rational comparison and arithmetic, and the selected affine function is an exact rational subgradient.  On the feasible region \(d>0\), \(|t|\le Ld\), (9) gives \(u^\star=t/d\), and direct substitution yields
\[
 \Phi_\theta(d,t)=\frac{(t-d\theta)^2}{d}.
\tag{10}
\]
At the feasible zero face, \(d=0\) forces \(t=0\), and (8) gives \(\Phi_\theta(0,0)=0\) without division.  Hence (8) is a global convex extension of exactly the closed perspective used by \(\mathsf P\).

Put
\[
 F(d,t)=\max_{\kappa\in\mathcal K}
 \sum_{n,\omega}H_{\kappa n\omega}
       \Phi_{\theta_\kappa}(d_n,t_{n\omega}).
\tag{11}
\]
At a rational query, calculate every summand by (8), choose a maximizing \(\kappa\), and sum its active affine subgradients.  This is an exact rational value-and-subgradient oracle for the globally convex function \(F\), with running time polynomial in the displayed table size and the query bit length.  In particular it is an approximate-value oracle of any requested accuracy.

We now state the weak-optimization result used below in its precise operational form.  The cited result \(\texttt{lem:weak-rational-convex-optimization}\) says that, for a rational full-dimensional convex body \(C\subset\mathbb R^p\) with a rational center \(x_0\) and rational radii \(0<r\le R\) satisfying
\[
 B_2(x_0,r)\subseteq C\subseteq B_2(x_0,R),
\tag{12}
\]
a polynomial-time weak-membership oracle and a polynomial-time rational approximate-value oracle for a convex function produce, for rational \(\xi,\zeta>0\), a rational \(x\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_2(x,C)\le\zeta,
 \qquad f(x)\le\min_{y\in C}f(y)+\xi.
\tag{13}
\]
The number of oracle and bit operations is polynomial in \(p\), the encoding lengths of the oracles, center and radii, \(\log(R/r)\), \(\log(1/\xi)\), and \(\log(1/\zeta)\); the output is rational of polynomial bit length.  Maximization of a concave function follows by applying the same assertion to its negative.  This is the only external optimization theorem used in the proof.

Let
\[
 e=\min\{\varepsilon,1\},
 \qquad C_0=1+4L^2,
 \qquad \eta=\frac{e}{128JC_0},
 \qquad \gamma=\frac{e}{128AC_0}.
\tag{14}
\]
In particular \(2J\eta<1\) and \(2A\gamma<1\).  Eliminate the last design coordinate by
\(d_J=1-\sum_{j<J}d_j\), and let \(p=J-1+M\).  The first optimization body is the rational polytope
\[
 C_{
m P}=\left\{(d_1,\ldots,d_{J-1},t):
 d_n\ge2\eta\ (1\le n\le J),\quad
 |t_{n\omega}|\le Ld_n\right\}\subset\mathbb R^p.
\tag{15}
\]
It is full dimensional.  Its rational center is
\[
 x_{
m P}=(1/J,\ldots,1/J,0,\ldots,0).
\tag{16}
\]
Set
\[
 \Delta_{
m P}=\frac1J-2\eta,
 \qquad
 \rho_{
m P}=\min\left\{\frac{\Delta_{
m P}}J,
             \frac{L}{J(1+LJ)}\right\},
 \qquad R_{
m P}=1+L.
\tag{17}
\]
All are positive rationals.  The slack at (16) of a lower-mass face is \(\Delta_{
m P}\); after elimination, its normal has Euclidean norm at most \(J\).  The slack of a decision face is \(L/J\), and its normal has norm at most \(1+LJ\).  Therefore the Euclidean ball of radius \(\rho_{
m P}\) about (16) lies in \(C_{
m P}\).  More explicitly, the following are rational, nested, full-dimensional polytopes:
\[
 I_{
m P}=\{x:\|x-x_{
m P}\|_\infty\le\rho_{
m P}/p\}
 \subseteq C_{
m P}
 \subseteq O_{
m P}=\{x:\|x-x_{
m P}\|_\infty\le R_{
m P}\},
\tag{18}
\]
and they certify
\[
 B_2(x_{
m P},\rho_{
m P}/p)
 \subseteq I_{
m P},
 \qquad
 O_{
m P}\subseteq B_2(x_{
m P},pR_{
m P}).
\tag{19}
\]
Membership and separation for (15) are exact rational linear-inequality calculations.  The center, all half-widths, and all radii in (16)--(19) have bit length polynomial in the rational input length, \(\log(J+1)\), and \(\log(1/e)\).  This verifies every geometric hypothesis of (12), without an implicit ball or an unnamed erosion.

\emph{Step 3: a global dual oracle and its explicit containing bodies.}
Represent an ambient query by \((\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_{A-1})\in\mathbb R^{A-1}\), with \(\pi_A=1-\sum_{k<A}\pi_k\); the coordinates need not be nonnegative when the oracle is queried.  For every \((n,\omega)\), define the affine rational functions
\[
 a_{n\omega}(\pi)=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega},\quad
 h_{n\omega}(\pi)=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega}\theta_\kappa,\quad
 q_{n\omega}(\pi)=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega}\theta_\kappa^2.
\tag{20}
\]
Define, on this entire affine ambient space,
\[
 B_n(\pi)=\sum_\omega\min_{u\in[-L,L]}
 \{a_{n\omega}(\pi)u^2-2h_{n\omega}(\pi)u+q_{n\omega}(\pi)\},
 \qquad G(\pi)=\min_nB_n(\pi).
\tag{21}
\]
Each expression in braces is affine in \(\pi\) for fixed \(u\).  Thus \(G\), being the infimum over the finite choice of \(n\) and the compact choices of all \(u\)'s, is globally concave.

The oracle for (21) is exact and rational at every rational ambient query.  In a cell with \(a>0\), evaluate the quadratic at the clipped stationary point
\[
 u^\star=\max\{-L,\min\{L,h/a\}\};
\tag{22}
\]
if \(a\le0\), evaluate its two endpoints and choose the smaller.  Choose a minimizing \(n\).  The resulting loss vector
\[
 g_\kappa=\sum_\omega H_{\kappa n\omega}(u^\star_{n\omega}-\theta_\kappa)^2
\tag{23}
\]
defines an affine function that equals \(G\) at the query and dominates \(G\) everywhere, so (23), after the affine elimination of \(\pi_A\), is an exact rational supergradient.  Consequently \(-G\) has a global exact rational value-and-subgradient oracle satisfying the cited weak-optimization specification.

On the simplex, every \(a_{n\omega}\ge0\).  If it is positive, \(h/a\) is a convex combination of numbers in \([-L,L]\), so clipping in (22) is inactive and completing the square gives the term \(q-h^2/a\).  If \(a=0\), nonnegativity of \(\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega}\) forces \(h=q=0\), and (21) gives zero without division.  Using (6), we therefore have exactly
\[
 G(\pi)=\min_n b_n(\pi)
 \quad\text{for every }\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal K),
\tag{24}
\]
including every zero-prior-likelihood face.

The second optimization body is the reduced, rational polytope
\[
 C_{\rm D}=\{(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_{A-1}):\pi_\kappa\ge2\gamma
 \text{ for }1\le\kappa\le A\}\subset\mathbb R^{A-1}.
\tag{25}
\]
Put \(p_{\rm D}=A-1\), let \(x_{\rm D}\) have all coordinates \(1/A\), and set
\[
 \Delta_{\rm D}=\frac1A-2\gamma,
 \qquad \rho_{\rm D}=\frac{\Delta_{\rm D}}A.
\tag{26}
\]
The first \(A-1\) lower faces have normal norm one and the eliminated last face has normal norm at most \(A\).  Hence the explicit rational nesting is
\[
 \begin{split}
 I_{\rm D}&=\{x:\|x-x_{\rm D}\|_\infty\le\rho_{\rm D}/p_{\rm D}\}
 \subseteq C_{\rm D}
 \subseteq O_{\rm D}=\{x:\|x-x_{\rm D}\|_\infty\le1\},\\
 B_2(x_{\rm D},\rho_{\rm D}/p_{\rm D})&\subseteq I_{\rm D},
 \qquad O_{\rm D}\subseteq B_2(x_{\rm D},p_{\rm D}).
 \end{split}
\tag{27}
\]
These centers and radii again have polynomial bit length.  Exact rational linear inequalities give membership and separation.  Thus (12)--(13) apply to \(-G\) on (25), with no division at an ambient or feasible zero face.

\emph{Step 4: explicit tolerances, exact feasibility repair, and certificates.}
Use the following rational accuracy ledger:
\[
 \xi=\beta=e/32,
 \qquad
 \zeta_{\rm P}=\min\left\{\frac{\eta}{2J},
       \frac{e}{128LJ(1+LJ)}\right\},
 \qquad
 \zeta_{\rm D}=\frac{\gamma}{2A}.
\tag{28}
\]
All denominators are nonzero by \(L>0\), and their bit lengths are polynomial in the input length, \(\log(A+J+1)\), and \(\log(1/e)\).  The first call to (13), with \(C=C_{\rm P}\), \(f=F\), and tolerances \((\xi,\zeta_{\rm P})\), returns a rational \((\widehat d,\widehat t)\).  Affine elimination makes \(\sum_n\widehat d_n=1\) exact.  If \((d^0,t^0)\in C_{\rm P}\) is within Euclidean distance \(\zeta_{\rm P}\), then, for \(n<J\), \(\widehat d_n\ge2\eta-\zeta_{\rm P}\), while
\[
 \widehat d_J\ge2\eta-J\zeta_{\rm P} \ge \frac32\eta.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus every \(\widehat d_n\ge\eta>0\).  Define the exact rational repair
\[
 d_n^{\rm r}=\widehat d_n,
 \qquad
 t_{n\omega}^{\rm r}=max\{-L\widehat d_n,
                   \min\{L\widehat d_n,\widehat t_{n\omega}\}\}.
\tag{30}
\]
This uses comparison and clipping only; it is exactly feasible for the original primal polytope.  From the nearby point in \(C_{\rm P}\), each clipped coordinate moves by at most
\[
 |t_{n\omega}^{\rm r}-\widehat t_{n\omega}|
 \le(1+LJ)\zeta_{\rm P}.
\tag{31}
\]
Indeed, the \(t\)-coordinate changes by at most \(\zeta_{\rm P}\), an uneliminated \(d_n\) by at most \(\zeta_{\rm P}\), and the eliminated \(d_J\) by at most \(J\zeta_{\rm P}\).

Every affine slope in (8) with respect to \(t\) has magnitude at most \(4L\).  By (6), summing this bound over \(\omega\) gives one for each \(n\).  Hence (28)--(31) imply
\[
 F(d^{\rm r},t^{\rm r})-F(\widehat d,\widehat t)
 \le4LJ(1+LJ)\zeta_{\rm P}\le e/32.
\tag{32}
\]

Let \((d^\star,t^\star)\) attain the unrestricted primal value, whose existence and equality to \(R^\star\) are supplied by \(\texttt{thm:endpoint-orbit-equivalence}\).  Set \(u_n=1/J\), use decision zero at \(u\), and mix with weight
\(\lambda_{\rm P}=2J\eta=e/(64C_0)\):
\[
 (d',t')=(1-\lambda_{\rm P})(d^\star,t^\star)
              +\lambda_{\rm P}(u,0).
\tag{33}
\]
Then \(d'_n\ge2\eta\), and convexity of (11), (6), and (7) give
\[
 \min_{C_{\rm P}}F
 \le F(d',t')
 \le(1-\lambda_{\rm P})R^\star+\lambda_{\rm P}L^2
 \le R^\star+e/64.
\tag{34}
\]
The \(e/64\) in (34) may be recorded as \(e/128\) for imposing \(d_n\ge\eta\) and \(e/128\) for the additional interior buffer to \(2\eta\); equation (33) proves their combined bound, rather than assuming a regular interior optimum.

Let \(U_0=F(d^{\rm r},t^{\rm r})\), evaluated exactly by (8), and outward-round on the rational grid \(\beta\):
\[
 \overline R=\beta\left\lceil U_0/\beta\right\rceil.
\tag{35}
\]
The weak-optimality error in (13), the repair bound (32), and (34)--(35) give
\[
 R^\star\le U_0\le R^\star+e/64+e/32+e/32,
 \qquad
 R^\star\le\overline R<R^\star+7e/64.
\tag{36}
\]
The left inequality holds because (30) is a feasible procedure and \(R^\star\) is the primal minimum.  Moreover, (35) is checked by verifying, for every \(\kappa\), the rational inequality
\[
 \sum_{n,\omega}H_{\kappa n\omega}
 \frac{(t^{\rm r}_{n\omega}-d_n^{\rm r}\theta_\kappa)^2}{d_n^{\rm r}}
 \le\overline R;
\tag{37}
\]
all denominators in (37) are positive by (29).  Thus the reported upper bound is independent of any unverified floating-point output.

For the dual call, mix an attaining prior \(\pi^\star\) with the uniform prior with weight
\(\lambda_{\rm D}=2A\gamma=e/(64C_0)\).  For every decision, its endpoint loss lies in \([0,4L^2]\).  Therefore changing a prior by total variation at most \(\lambda_{\rm D}\) changes its expected loss by at most \(4L^2\lambda_{\rm D}\le C_0\lambda_{\rm D}\).  Taking the infimum over decisions preserves this inequality, and the mixed prior belongs to \(C_{\rm D}\).  Using (24) and endpoint minimax duality gives
\[
 \max_{\pi\in C_{\rm D}}G(\pi)\ge R^\star-e/64.
\tag{38}
\]
Apply (13) to \(-G\) with \((\xi,\zeta_{\rm D})\), obtaining rational \(\widehat\pi\).  The reduced coordinates sum to one exactly.  Proximity to (25) implies that each of the first \(A-1\) coordinates is at least \(2\gamma-\zeta_{\rm D}>0\), and the last is at least
\(2\gamma-A\zeta_{\rm D}=3\gamma/2\).  Thus \(\widehat\pi\) is already an exactly feasible prior; no numerical projection or division is used.  Let \(V_0=G(\widehat\pi)\), evaluated exactly by (21), and set
\[
 \underline R=\beta\left\lfloor V_0/\beta\right\rfloor.
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (13), (38), and (39) imply
\[
 \underline R>R^\star-e/64-e/32-e/32
 =R^\star-5e/64.
\tag{40}
\]
For a direct dual check, compute (20) exactly.  If \(a_{n\omega}>0\), set
\(\rho_{n\omega}=h_{n\omega}^2/a_{n\omega}\); if \(a_{n\omega}=0\), exact rational comparison detects it and one sets \(\rho_{n\omega}=0\).  The implication \(a=0\Rightarrow h=0\) proved above verifies every rotated-cone zero face.  Equation (39) is precisely the finite list
\[
 \underline R\le
 \sum_\kappa\widehat\pi_\kappa\theta_\kappa^2
       -\sum_\omega\rho_{n\omega}
 \quad(n\in\mathcal N),
\tag{41}
\]
so it is a feasible rational certificate for \(\mathsf Q\) and therefore \(\underline R\le R^\star\).

For clarity, the complete additive ledger, in units of \(e/128\), is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{operation}&\text{upper side}&\text{lower side}\\ \hline
\text{restriction to mass at least }\eta\text{ or }\gamma&1&1\\
\text{buffer from }\eta\text{ or }\gamma\text{ to twice that mass}&1&1\\
\text{weak optimization value error}&4&4\\
\text{near-feasibility repair or clipping}&4&0\\
\text{exact evaluation followed by outward grid rounding}&4&4
\end{array}
\tag{42}
\]
The first two rows are jointly certified by (34) and (38); the dual proximity buffer makes the returned point exactly feasible and hence costs no additional objective error.  Exact evaluation itself costs zero; the displayed four units are solely the explicit outward rounding in (35) and (39).  Thus (36) and (40) actually give
\[
 0\le\overline R-\underline R<12e/64=3e/16<e\le\varepsilon.
\tag{43}
\]

The two oracle calls have dimensions at most the displayed program size.  Their radius ratios are given explicitly in (17)--(19) and (26)--(27).  Equations (14) and (28) show that the logarithms of their inverse radii and tolerances are polynomial in the rational input bit length, \(\log(A+J+M+1)\), and \(\log\max\{2,1/\varepsilon\}\).  The exact oracle evaluations use a polynomial number of additions, multiplications, comparisons, and divisions of polynomial-bit rationals.  Exact evaluation of (37) and (41) has polynomial bit complexity as well: adding at most the displayed number of rational terms increases numerator and denominator bit lengths by at most the sum of their polynomial bit lengths.  The cited weak-optimization result now proves the asserted Turing running-time and output-bit bounds.  Notice that only rational approximate points were requested; no exact optimizer was asserted rational.

\emph{Step 5: implementable randomization and a total division-free decoder.}
The rational masses \(d_n^{\rm r}\) define an exact sampling rule: sample an assignment histogram by integer cumulative weights after clearing their denominators, allocate its labels uniformly to equal-size labeled clusters, and sample each feasible treated subset independently and uniformly conditional on its label.  Rejection sampling from a power-of-two interval samples each required rational finite law exactly with expected polynomially many bit operations.  By \(\texttt{thm:endpoint-orbit-equivalence}\), this is the implementable correlated design represented by the primal point.

Precompute the rational endpoint table by
\[
 \delta_{n\omega}=t^{\rm r}_{n\omega}/d_n^{\rm r}.
\tag{44}
\]
The denominator is positive by (29), and (30) proves \(|\delta_{n\omega}|\le L\).  More generally, when decoding any feasible face of \(\mathsf P\), set \(\delta_{n\omega}=0\) if \(d_n=0\); feasibility then forces \(t_{n\omega}=0\).  For the dual posterior table use \(h/a\) only when exact comparison gives \(a>0\), and use zero when \(a=0\).  Thus every discrete table is total before continuous outcomes are considered.

Fix a realized labeled assignment \(x\), and let \(v_{gi}\in[0,1]\) be its revealed outcome coordinates.  Order the units in cluster \(g\), put \(z_{gi}=\mathbf 1\{i\in S_g\}\), and initialize \(Q_{g,0}(0,0)=1\), with all other states zero.  For \(1\le j\le s_g\), use the explicit recursion
\[
 Q_{g,j}(u,w)=(1-v_{gj})Q_{g,j-1}(u,w)
 +v_{gj}Q_{g,j-1}(u-z_{gj},w-(1-z_{gj})),
\tag{45}
\]
where a negative-index state is zero.  Thus \(Q_{g,s_g}(u,w)\) is exactly the Bernoulli-rounding probability of local category \((A_g,u,w)\).

Order the clusters and let \(e_{j,u,w}\) be one unit in the histogram coordinate indexed by \((s_j,A_j,u,w)\).  Initialize \(T_0(0)=1\), with other states zero, and set
\[
 T_j(h)=\sum_{u=0}^{r_{s_j,A_j}}\sum_{w=0}^{s_j-r_{s_j,A_j}}
 T_{j-1}(h-e_{j,u,w})Q_{j,s_j}(u,w),
 \qquad 1\le j\le m,
\tag{46}
\]
again assigning zero to an absent state.  Then \(T_m(\omega)\) is the probability of binary observation histogram \(\omega\), and the decoder is
\[
 \overline\delta(x,v)=\sum_{\omega}T_m(\omega)\delta_{n(x),\omega}.
\tag{47}
\]
Equations (45)--(47) use only addition, subtraction, and multiplication after the rational constants (44) have been installed; in particular, the evaluation circuit contains no division.  There are only boundedly many local states per cluster, and (46) retains at most the displayed number of observation-histogram states, so its circuit size is polynomial in the displayed orbit size and the labeled input length.  For rational \(v\), exact rational arithmetic gives exact evaluation and detects \(T_m(\omega)=0\) by testing its reduced numerator.  Its bit complexity is polynomial in the circuit size and the total bit length of the rational inputs.  No assertion is made that an arbitrary real number has a finite Turing encoding.  Separately, (45)--(47) are finite polynomials, so the same circuit defines a total mathematical function for every real \(v\in\mathbb R^N\); only on \([0,1]^N\) is it used as a Bernoulli expectation and as the estimator.

Finally, expanding the recursion shows
\[
 \overline\delta(x,v)=
 \sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal O(x)}}
 \delta_{[x,e]}
 \prod_{j:e_j=1}v_j\prod_{j:e_j=0}(1-v_j),
\tag{48}
\]
which is exactly the multilinear extension in \(\texttt{def:endpoint-extension}\).  The endpoint theorem therefore turns (37) into the same upper bound over every bounded real schedule, while the rational binary prior in (41) remains a valid lower bound for that larger nature class.  This proves all parts of the compiler claim, including boundary treated counts, label-constant menus, and all zero-probability faces.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomized saturation experiments expose overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither the no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a constant treated-count menu, admits an exact reduction of worst-case mean squared error over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators to a rational endpoint orbit game. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, and independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite primal-dual characterization. The rational two-cluster, size-three certificate gives a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The orbit game is algorithmic in the Turing model: explicit global rational oracles and rational inner and outer polytopes yield polynomial-time weak primal-dual optimization, outward-rounded risk certificates, and a total division-free continuous-estimator decoder, without claiming rational exact optimizers.

project_justification.fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation. It gives a finite independent-design frontier, a strict rational separation certificate, and a bit-certified compiler whose explicit global perspective and bounded-decision oracles return checkable rational \(\varepsilon\)-saddles and a total zero-face-safe decoder in time polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size, input bit length, and \(\log\max\{2,1/\varepsilon\}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators. BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 provides the motivating fixed-count randomized-saturation design and its direct and spillover analysis, but not an unrestricted finite-population minimax estimator or a bit-certified joint design algorithm. Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy design optimality at a general decision-theoretic level, while the present result constructs and weakly optimizes the exact rational observation-hypergraph quotient. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies a different pairwise conflict-graph design problem and gives a polynomial approximation there; the present kernel retains higher-order exact-count observation compatibility. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 supply endpoint reductions in no-interference experiments, whereas the present compiler covers bounded anonymous saturation interference, arbitrary correlated first-stage laws, boundary treated counts, and label-constant menus. HudgensHalloran2008, BasseFeller2018, and JiangImaiMalani2023 provide the design-based two-stage causal framework but do not jointly optimize over arbitrary estimators and correlated saturation laws.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a fixed menu of saturation labels and bounded cluster sizes, an experimental team can compile the exact finite observation experiment rather than approximate it by pairwise conflicts. The output is operational: rational weights specify how to randomize saturation histograms and treated subsets, the endpoint table specifies a possibly nonlinear analysis rule, and two independently checkable rational inequalities bracket the worst-case causal mean-squared error within any requested rational tolerance. The continuous-outcome rule is a finite Bernoulli-histogram polynomial, so structurally impossible or prior-null observations never trigger an undefined posterior ratio.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The compiler guarantee is polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size for fixed \(K\) and \(b\); it does not make the constant-size response alphabet small in practice and does not give a strongly polynomial algorithm. Exact rational arithmetic can produce large certificates even though their bit length is polynomial. The numerical size-three witness remains supported by its separate exhaustive rational verifier, while the general compiler theorem supplies the symbolic kernel construction, oracle geometry, tolerance accounting, and decoder proof rather than a new numerical rerun.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, the exact orbit game, and the bit-certified compiler cover every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant treated-count menus. The compiler returns rational \(\varepsilon\)-optimal primal and dual certificates and a total continuous estimator; it does not claim that exact optimizers are rational, an elementary closed-form classification of the independent-saturation frontier, or a separation as the number of clusters tends to infinity. The strict advantage remains the certified two-cluster instance and its infinite rational contrast neighborhood, and its proof uses the full exact-count observation hypergraph.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem makes the finite minimax reduction deployable and auditable: every approximation, feasibility repair, zero face, and outward rounding step has an explicit rational certificate.
statement_notes.gap: Existing design-minimax and network-experiment algorithms do not provide this exact observation-hypergraph orbit compiler with global rational perspective and Bayes-risk oracles, explicit rational well-bounding polytopes, and a total nonlinear decoder.
statement_notes.consumer: A randomized-saturation experiment can archive an exact kernel, an implementable correlated randomization, a nonlinear analysis table, and a machine-checkable risk interval of any prescribed rational width.
